questions.question_text: A licensee posts a property listing on social media without mentioning the brokerage. Under Rea 404.05, what type of ad is this?
distractors: A compliant digital ad
An exempt personal post
A permissible team ad
questions.explanation: Under Rea 404.05(b) and RSA 331-A:16, IV, an advertisement of real estate for another must prominently include the brokerage firm's name (or the principal broker's name). An ad that omits brokerage identification is a prohibited blind ad. For space-limited electronic media, RSA 331-A:16, IV(c) allows compliance through a link to an Internet display containing the required information — but a social media post with no brokerage identification and no such link violates the rule.

questions.question_text: What must every real estate advertisement in New Hampshire include under Rea 404.05?
distractors: The property's asking price
The MLS listing number
The OPLC license number
questions.explanation: Rea 404.05(b) requires every advertisement of real estate for another to prominently include the name of the brokerage firm with which the licensee is associated, or the licensee's principal broker's name. RSA 331-A:16, IV(a) separately requires the advertising licensee's own legal name and the firm name to be clearly identifiable, across all advertising media.

questions.question_text: A real estate team wants to advertise under their team name. Which statement about NH advertising rules is correct?
questions.correct_answer: Team names must include brokerage ID
distractors: Team names fully replace the brokerage ID
Team ads are completely exempt from rules
Teams cannot advertise separately at all
questions.explanation: Team advertising is permitted in New Hampshire, but RSA 331-A:16, IV(b) requires any advertising containing direct contact information for a licensee or a team of licensees to also include the name and telephone number of the individual principal broker or brokerage firm. The team name never replaces the brokerage identification required by Rea 404.05.

questions.question_text: A broker publishes a newspaper ad for a listing. Which element is required for compliance with NH advertising rules?
questions.correct_answer: Brokerage name as it is licensed
distractors: Agent's personal phone number
Listing price and square footage
Commission rate offered to buyers
questions.explanation: Under Rea 404.05, every advertisement must contain the brokerage name as licensed. There is no requirement to include the agent's phone number, property details, or commission information for the ad to be compliant.

questions.question_text: An agent argues that internet ads have different rules than print ads in NH. Is this correct?
questions.correct_answer: No, same rules apply to all media
distractors: Yes, internet ads are less strict
Yes, internet ads need more detail
Yes, social media is fully exempt
questions.explanation: New Hampshire applies the same advertising rules to all media: RSA 331-A:16, IV(a) applies to all categories of advertising, including publications, radio and television broadcasts, electronic media, electronic mail, and the Internet. The only accommodation is RSA 331-A:16, IV(c), which lets space-limited electronic media comply through a link to an Internet display containing the required information.

questions.question_text: Under RSA 331-A:16, what is required for a brokerage to operate a branch office in New Hampshire?
distractors: Only a written notice filed to OPLC
Formal approval from the local MLS board
Registration with the municipal town clerk
questions.explanation: Under RSA 331-A:16, I, a principal broker must submit a branch office application form to the OPLC before opening any branch office and must designate a managing broker for each branch. The branch itself is licensed: Rea 301.01(e) requires a broker license as a firm branch, and Rea 305.03 provides for firm branch license certificates naming the managing broker.

questions.question_text: A principal broker opens a second office location. Who must be assigned to supervise the branch under RSA 331-A:16?
distractors: Any active salesperson
The original office manager
A REALTOR association member
questions.explanation: Under RSA 331-A:16, I, the principal broker shall designate a managing broker for each branch office, and under RSA 331-A:16, II all licensees and employees must be reasonably supervised by the principal broker or managing broker. A managing broker is defined in RSA 331-A:2, VI as a broker who manages a branch office. If the position becomes vacant, RSA 331-A:16-a permits a temporary manager for up to one year.

questions.question_text: A brokerage operates three branch offices. How many branch licenses does NH require?
distractors: One license covers all branches
Two licenses plus main office
No branch license is needed
questions.explanation: Each branch office requires its own application and firm branch license: RSA 331-A:16, I requires a branch office application before opening any branch office, and Rea 301.01(e) and Rea 301.02(a) provide for a broker license as a firm branch with its own fee and renewal. Three branch offices therefore require three firm branch licenses in addition to the main office license.

questions.question_text: Which scenario violates NH branch office requirements?
distractors: Branch with its own separate license
Branch with a designated managing broker
Branch filing its own separate annual reports
questions.explanation: Each branch office must have a designated managing broker under RSA 331-A:16, I, and all licensees and employees must be reasonably supervised by the principal broker or managing broker under RSA 331-A:16, II. Operating a branch without supervisory oversight violates these requirements and is prohibited conduct under RSA 331-A:26, XXVII.

questions.question_text: A salesperson wants to work from a home office and meet clients there regularly. What must the brokerage do under NH law?
questions.correct_answer: License it as a branch office
distractors: File a home office exemption form
Register with the local town office
No action is required by the broker
questions.explanation: A branch office is defined in RSA 331-A:2, II as a real estate broker's office other than the principal place of business. A home office used regularly to conduct brokerage business and meet clients operates as an office of the firm, so the principal broker must submit a branch office application and designate a managing broker under RSA 331-A:16, I before it opens. New Hampshire has no home-office exemption form.
